requirements: Adopt a shared governance/runtime record envelope across first-class record families with stable identity, scope, status, timestamps, refs, and lineage links.
Keep canonical records structurally distinct from artifacts/rendered outputs, with artifacts linked by canonical refs rather than substituting record identity.
Define separate but mappable lifecycle models for orchestration lanes and concrete worktrees, including explicit cleanup eligibility and historical survivability after live removal.
Gate archive/prune/remove actions on active ownership, blocked recovery dependencies, safe-point restore needs, unresolved conflict workflows, and downstream lineage dependencies.
Expand canonical glossary/help ownership to new orchestrator concepts and high-risk term distinctions to prevent cross-surface copy drift.
Preserve shared requested/effective runtime identity semantics across conversational/document-production surfaces while preventing ontology collapse into orchestrator execution objects.
Define orchestrator export taxonomy (`record`, `bundle`, `view`) with manifest requirements and trust-state disclosure/revalidation for projection-derived exports.
Route notifications/escalations using combined dimensions (severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, projection trust) instead of severity-only logic.
decisions: Use a shared envelope + family payload pattern rather than ad hoc top-level record shapes per governance object.
Treat lane lifecycle and worktree lifecycle as related but non-identical state machines.
Retain historical identity/lineage after archive/prune/remove; cleanup affects live backing, not history/ledger truth.
Anchor glossary as canonical short-definition source; let help provide deeper examples and related concept links.
Formalize boundary rule: shared runtime identity does not imply shared execution ontology.
Classify exports explicitly as canonical records, portable bundles, or derived views to avoid semantic ambiguity in JSON/CSV outputs.
Require manifest trust disclosure or canonical refresh when exporting from stale/degraded projections.
Use concern acknowledgment for noise control only; do not allow it to suppress still-active blocked states.
routing_rules: Source Control remains worktree-first and compact; Orchestrator carries richer lane lineage/policy context with worktree status attached.
Default Source Control visibility focuses live/current rows; retained/cleanup-eligible/historical materials are filter/toggle scoped.
Notification destination is owner-aware: user-owned blocks can route to chat/progress/system notifications; operational owner blocks route to operational surfaces first.
History is canonical chronology; Progress/Dashboard handles active attention; thread/chat handles direct user action paths; system notification is sparse summon layer.
verification_rules: Before destructive cleanup actions verify no active run ownership and no unresolved recovery/safe-point/lineage dependency on the target worktree/lane.
Ensure archive/prune/remove preserve inspectable historical records in History/Ledger/lineage views.
When projection trust is stale/degraded, either qualify notification/export claims with trust disclosure or re-query canonical backing data.
Validate JSON export semantics against taxonomy: canonical record payload vs filtered view dump vs bundle manifest package.
owner_consumer_obligations: Orchestrator owners define lane-pool truth, cleanup posture, and policy explanations.
Source Control owners execute concrete worktree operations and present compact operational inventory.
Glossary/help owners maintain canonical terminology and distinction guidance across surfaces.
Runtime identity consumers (chat/interview/builders/orchestrator) must reuse requested/effective disclosure grammar without collapsing object identities.
Notification system owners enforce escalation policy dimensions and trust-aware confidence language.
stale_retirement_items: Retire ad hoc governance record top-level shapes in favor of shared envelope + payload families.
Retire ambiguous cleanup semantics where archive/prune/remove are treated as equivalent operations.
Retire glossary gaps that permit synonym drift for lane/worktree, history/ledger, historical/superseded, and related pairs.
Retire overconfident projection-derived alerts/exports that do not disclose stale/degraded trust state.
open_questions: What exact schema contract and versioning policy will govern the shared envelope and per-family payload extensibility?
What authoritative mapping table should govern lane-state to worktree-state transitions across recovery and cleanup flows?
Which export surfaces require mandatory manifests vs optional manifests, and how strict should trust-state fields be for simple record exports?
What thresholds and timing policies should drive owner-based escalation to system notifications across blocked categories?
process_defects: Documentation currently defines many components but leaves key interaction policies implicit across seams.
Export semantics are distributed across domains, creating ambiguity about canonical vs derived JSON outputs.
Terminology governance lags behind orchestrator rewrite velocity, increasing copy and UX drift risk.
Notification policy lacks explicit combined-dimension routing logic despite existing severity ladders and trust-state needs.
